issue.title: bob capture --dry-run prints 'would savefile/…': clip confirmation verb column is exactly as wide as 'would save'

task_type_fields.impact: Cosmetic: every dry-run %c attachment or snippet confirmation runs the verb into the path, which hurts the human output's readability.
task_type_fields.repro:
```bash
T=$(mktemp -d); printf -- '---\ntype: "[[area]]"\nparent: "[[area]]"\n---\n# Mac Inbox\n\n## Tasks\n' > $T/mac_inbox.md
BOB_CLIPBOARD_CMD="echo $HOME/tmp/screencasts/20261116_155943.mp4" bob capture -b $T --dry-run 'x %c'
# → "[dry-run] ok would savefile/20261116_155943.mp4"   (no space between verb and path)
```

**Root cause:** `print_clip_file_confirmation` formats `{verb:<10}` (`src/native/capture/output.rs:7340`), and `"would save"` is exactly 10 characters, so nothing pads it. Widening the field to 11 (or adding a literal space) fixes it. Update any golden test that pins the old column.

issue.creation_reason: Cosmetic defect noticed while dry-running %c attachments for the video-embed research; the root cause is a one-character pad width.

evidence.note: Independent root-cause confirmation by the research.63 lead consolidator on current master: src/native/capture/output.rs:7333 defines the verb 'would save' (exactly 10 chars) and :7340 formats it as {verb:<10}, so the pad width adds no separator before the saved path. Widening to 11 or adding a literal space fixes it, as the bead says.
